correctness.rationale: With normalized coordinates \(u=cx,v=y\), every nontrivial \(G^2\)-fixed point satisfies \(u_1=-u_0\ne0\) and hence \(g(v_0)=g(v_1)=-1\). This forces \(v_1=-v_0\), \(a<-2\), and the unique orbit. The Jacobian \(J=\begin{pmatrix}-1&-8t^2/(1+t^2)\\1&1\end{pmatrix}\) has \(J^2=((1-7t^2)/(1+t^2))I_2=(-7-16/a)I_2\). Smooth hyperbolic theory gives the stated local stability intervals; the exact nonzero return Hessian at \(a=-16/7\) establishes quadratic superattraction. Exact symbolic verification passed; no finite enumeration is used to prove exhaustiveness.
